fixes.explanation: Right, friend. The letter says, "Abstain from every form of evil." (1 Thessalonians 5:22) Just before it comes "…test all things. Hold fast to what is good." (1 Thessalonians 5:21) So good gets the grip, and evil gets the cold shoulder. Every form means every form, not just the big ones.

Yes, friend. The letter says, "The One who calls you is faithful, and He will do it." (1 Thessalonians 5:24) The "it" is the sanctifying and keeping blameless from the verse before. The letter puts that big job on the One who calls. That's a relief, because I couldn't carry that batch myself.

Yes, friend. The writers ask the brothers to "…acknowledge those who work diligently among you, who care for you in the Lord and who admonish you." (1 Thessalonians 5:12) That's three jobs in one sentence: working hard, caring and admonishing. The letter says to notice the people doing them.

Nope, no city officials in this verse, friend. The writers point to people right among the brothers, those who "…work diligently among you…" (1 Thessalonians 5:12) These are folks who care for the brothers in the Lord and admonish them. The next verse says to hold them in highest regard because of their work. (1 Thessalonians 5:13)

Not quite, friend. The writers aren't pointing far away at all. They point to those "among you," the ones who work diligently, care for the brothers in the Lord and admonish them. (1 Thessalonians 5:12) Jerusalem doesn't come up in this passage, so the hard workers are right there with the brothers.

Yes, friend. The letter says, "Make sure that no one repays evil for evil." (1 Thessalonians 5:15) Notice it says no one, so it's a job for the whole group. Put the phone down, friend, and leave that reply unsent.

Good guess, but the letter doesn't say that here. It says, "Make sure that no one repays evil for evil." (1 Thessalonians 5:15) The command is aimed at the brothers themselves, and it says nothing about handing the problem off. So that's on all of us, and I'd better keep my mustache off the keyboard.

This one is true, friend, and I know it sounds like too much. The verse says, "Give thanks in every circumstance, for this is God’s will for you in Christ Jesus." (1 Thessalonians 5:18) Every circumstance, no exceptions listed, and it's tied to God's will for them in Christ Jesus. I'd check the verse twice too, but it says what it says.

Right, friend. It isn't only the soul. The letter says, "…may your entire spirit, soul, and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ." (1 Thessalonians 5:23) The whole person is covered, and that's good news for every one of us.

Yes, friend. The writer says, "I charge you before the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers." (1 Thessalonians 5:27) Charged before the Lord, so it's no small request. The letter is meant to be read to all the brothers.

This one is true, friend. The writer says, "I charge you before the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers." (1 Thessalonians 5:27) Charged before the Lord, and the reading is for all the brothers. The card says exactly that.
